title: Maximum XOR of Two Numbers
description: Given an integer array `nums`, return the maximum result of `nums[i] XOR nums[j]`, where `0 <= i <= j < n`.
input_format: First line contains integer `n`, followed by `n` integers.
hints: Build max XOR greedily bit by bit from most significant (bit 30) down to 0.
Check if desired candidate prefix can be formed by two prefixes: `p1 ^ p2 == candidate <=> p1 ^ candidate == p2`.
Can also be solved using a binary Trie.

reference_solution:
import sys
data = sys.stdin.read().split()
if data:
    n = int(data[0])
    nums = [int(x) for x in data[1:1+n]]
    max_xor = 0
    mask = 0
    for i in range(30, -1, -1):
        mask |= (1 << i)
        prefixes = {num & mask for num in nums}
        candidate = max_xor | (1 << i)
        if any((candidate ^ p) in prefixes for p in prefixes):
            max_xor = candidate
    print(max_xor)
